clue.text: Realise obsessive political analyst is upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, being upset means turned upside down, so the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a wonk is someone obsessed with the details of policy

explanation.surface: Someone discovers that a policy-obsessed pundit is distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is upset' turns WONK over in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise something is to come to be aware of it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: One who makes short work of a link with ringleader

parts.note: a bridge is a link between two places
read as the leader of 'ring', its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone deals quickly with a connection to the head of a gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringleader' is read as two words: the leader, or first letter, of 'ring'.
explanation.definitionFit: An abridger shortens texts, so literally makes works shorter; a witty pun on the idiom.

clue.text: Squander money in way that's sad and obscene

definitions.meaning: in British slang to ... money is to spend it recklessly
a ... joke or film is a smutty one

explanation.surface: Wasting cash in a manner that is both pitiful and indecent.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses of one colour word: British slang for spending wastefully, low in spirits, and smutty.

clue.text: Lord revealing what every schoolboy should know

definitions.text: Lord revealing what every schoolboy should know

parts.words: Lord revealing what every schoolboy should know
parts.note: the historian peer famous for the phrase 'every schoolboy knows', used to introduce facts he thought obvious

explanation.walkthrough: The Victorian historian Thomas Babington, Lord Macaulay, often wrote 'every schoolboy knows'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian historian and peer is the lord who popularised the stock phrase about schoolboy knowledge.

clue.text: Blanket for victim of bombing

definitions.meaning: a knitted or crocheted blanket or throw
a person from Afghanistan, a country heavily bombed in the war of the time

explanation.surface: A cover offered to someone hurt in an air raid.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a crocheted woollen throw and a native of the bombed country.

clue.text: Choose distorted interpretation and get taken for a ride?

parts.note: to go for something is to choose it
a spin is a slanted interpretation put on events by a press officer

explanation.surface: Picking a slanted account of events, and so being cheated.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful definition: going for a spin is literally being taken for a ride in a car, not being swindled.
explanation.definitionFit: Going for a spin is a short pleasure drive, literally a ride; the idiom of being deceived misleads.

clue.text: RAF set out to deliver air attack

indicators.note: set out is read as letters thrown out of place, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: The Royal Air Force sets off to launch a raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges RAF and SET.
explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is to attack ground targets from low-flying aircraft with guns.

clue.text: Possible withdrawal from Mideast? That's a thought

indicators.note: a withdrawal from the word is letters drawn out of it, so the answer sits inside it

explanation.surface: Wondering whether troops might pull out of the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possible withdrawal from' takes letters out of the middle of Mideast.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a single thought or notion, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Explosives expert and arms manufacturer oddly responsible for 20 31

definitions.text: Explosives expert and arms manufacturer oddly responsible for 20 31

parts.words: Explosives expert and arms manufacturer oddly responsible for 20 31
parts.note: the Swedish inventor of dynamite, who owned the arms firm Bofors, founded a peace award, which is the oddity

explanation.walkthrough: 20 31 is PEACE PRIZE; Alfred Nobel invented dynamite and made arms, yet founded the peace award.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Nobel invented dynamite, owned an armaments company and endowed the prizes in his will.

clue.text: Offended one FBI operative about political group

parts.note: a is one

indicators.note: the agent goes about, around, the political group

parts.note: a Fed is an American federal agent
a front is a political movement, as in National Front

explanation.surface: Someone is insulted when a federal agent investigates a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container; the FBI agent's slang name wraps the political group, after the one.
explanation.definitionFit: Affronted means insulted or offended, a close synonym.

clue.text: As starter of war, what he is wanting arranged?

definitions.text: As starter of war, what he is wanting arranged?

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its opening letter
arranged says the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A war-starting leader wants his record made to look tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' signals the anagram after the war's first letter. Read whole, a leader who began a war wants the inquiry into it to be a cover-up, recalling the Iraq inquiries.
explanation.definitionFit: A whitewash is a cover-up clearing someone of blame, here what a warmonger would want arranged.

clue.text: One entitled to 9 20 31 if 17 20?

parts.note: the clue reads as one with a right to the Nobel Peace Prize if war is peace, a jibe at a leader who won it while waging war

explanation.walkthrough: 9 20 31 is NOBEL PEACE PRIZE, 17 20 is WAR IS PEACE; the US president won the prize in 2009 while still at war.
explanation.definitionFit: The US president was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2009 while commanding wars abroad.

clue.text: Having wise men leading Western state would be wonderful!

indicators.note: the wise men lead, coming before, the state

parts.note: the Magi are the wise men of the Nativity story
Cal is an abbreviation for California, a western US state

explanation.surface: With the three wise men in charge of a western state, it would be marvellous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading' puts the wise men first; Cal is a standard short form of California.
explanation.definitionFit: Magical means enchanting or marvellous, a synonym for wonderful.

clue.text: Cut nothing in false English WMD version

indicators.note: the nothing goes in the shuffled letters
false says the letters are not in their true order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: O, the figure zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: A false English version of the weapons story cuts out nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'false' rearranges E and WMD into MWED, and 'in' puts O inside to give MOWED.
explanation.definitionFit: Mowed is a past form meaning cut, as grass is cut by a mower.

clue.text: Reach GIs in disarray, moving from military position

indicators.note: in disarray puts the letters into disorder, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Soldiers arrive in a mess as they withdraw from a post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is part of the fodder, so 'disarray' alone signals the anagram of REACH GIS IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashiering an officer is dismissing them from the forces, removing them from their post.

clue.text: Clear about deity supporting war? That's most convenient

indicators.note: the clear amount goes about, around, the god

parts.note: net, as of profit, is the clear amount after deductions
Ares is the Greek god of war

explanation.surface: A clear sum about a god backing a war is the handiest option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the net amount round the Greek war god; 'supporting war' describes the deity, not a position.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearest means closest at hand, hence handiest; a sense extended from distance to convenience.

clue.text: Extremes of terror, aim of roughly defined movement

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: an end is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: The goal of terror is a general drift that is only loosely outlined.
explanation.definitionFit: A trend is a general direction of change, a movement without precise limits.

clue.text: Literary paradox making Tolstoy's work redundant

parts.note: if the slogan were true, the Russian novel of conflict and calm would be a needless title, its two halves being the same thing

explanation.surface: An Orwellian contradiction renders a classic Russian novel pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: The slogan is from Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four; if the two are the same, War and Peace says one thing twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The Party slogan in Nineteen Eighty-Four is a self-contradicting statement from a novel.

clue.text: Fictional agreement given to minister, then PM

definitions.text: Fictional agreement given to minister, then PM

parts.words: Fictional agreement given to minister, then PM
parts.note: the BBC sitcom where a civil servant agreed with a minister, and its sequel when he became Prime Minister

explanation.walkthrough: Yes Minister and Yes, Prime Minister were BBC sitcoms about a minister and his scheming civil servant.
explanation.definitionFit: The word of assent is the title word of the sitcoms in which a minister later becomes Prime Minister.

clue.text: According to Party slogan, 27 is such power

parts.words: According to Party slogan, 27 is such
parts.note: in Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four the Party slogan says ignorance equals this quality

explanation.surface: The Party claims a lack of knowledge is a kind of might.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 is IGNORANCE; the Party in Nineteen Eighty-Four proclaims 'Ignorance is Strength'.
explanation.definitionFit: Strength is power or might, a straight synonym.

clue.text: See 17
Main area that divides Europe and US

definitions.meaning: the main is an old word for the open sea, and this is an area of it
the ocean lying between Europe and America

explanation.surface: A key region that splits Europe from America.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocean separating Europe and America is a vast stretch of sea, poetically the main.

clue.text: Collection of documents found to be dodgy ie dross

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Papers are exposed as a dodgy heap of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' rearranges IE and DROSS; the surface recalls the 2003 'dodgy dossier' on Iraq.
explanation.definitionFit: A dossier is a file of papers on a person or subject.

clue.text: Lots of flights contributing to worst air strikes

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Many sorties are part of the most damaging bombing raids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contributing to' finds the answer across worST AIR Strikes.
explanation.definitionFit: Stairs are flights of steps, so a set of them means lots of flights; flights as aircraft sorties misleads.

clue.text: Disclosure in editorials partly controlled

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Revelations in leading articles were kept in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' finds the answer across disclosuRE IN EDitorials.
explanation.definitionFit: Reined, as a horse is reined in, means held in check or controlled.

clue.text: Offensive commanded caused anger

parts.note: rank means foul or offensive
led means commanded, as troops are led

explanation.surface: An offensive that was ordered stirred up resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offensive' looks like a military attack but is an adjective meaning foul.
explanation.definitionFit: Rankled means caused lasting irritation or resentment.

clue.text: Orwell's name for one elected just before 1984

definitions.meaning: George Orwell was the pen name of Eric Arthur ...
the future Labour PM first became an MP in 1983

explanation.surface: The author's real surname belongs to someone voted in on the eve of his famous year.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's real surname is shared by the Labour leader first elected to Parliament in 1983.

clue.text: World leader, so-called

parts.note: the US president nicknamed Dubya, for W, the leader or first letter of World, his middle initial

explanation.walkthrough: George W. Bush was nicknamed 'Dubya' after his middle initial W, the leader of 'World'.
explanation.definitionFit: The US president at the time of the Iraq War was known by his initial W.

clue.text: Not a valid defence for a Niger con when demolished

indicators.note: demolished means knocked down and broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fraud over Niger cannot be excused once exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when demolished' rearranges A NIGER CON; the surface recalls the forged Niger uranium claims about Iraq.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorance of the law is famously no excuse, so not knowing is not a valid defence.

clue.text: Flawed conclusions used by warmonger to drop diplomacy

indicators.note: the conclusions of words are their final letters

explanation.surface: A warmonger reaches faulty conclusions to abandon diplomacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conclusions' takes the last letters of the four words.
explanation.definitionFit: Ropy is British informal for poor in quality or shoddy, hence flawed.

clue.text: Former PM at centre of belated enquiry

indicators.note: at the centre of these words sits a run of letters spanning them

explanation.surface: A past premier is the focus of a long-delayed investigation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at centre of' finds the answer in belatED ENquiry; Anthony Eden was the British PM of the Suez crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Eden was British Prime Minister from 1955 to 1957.

clue.text: Harsh way in which torture results, primarily, in limited information

indicators.note: the other pieces sit in the abbreviation for way

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: primarily takes the first letters of the words

parts.note: gen is British slang for information, here a short word for it

explanation.surface: A severe method by which torture yields only scant intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which' signals the container: torture's and results' first letters, 'in' as written and slang for information all go inside the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringent means strict or severe, close to harsh.

clue.text: Value force, from what we hear

indicators.note: what we hear signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: to prise is to force open with a lever

explanation.surface: Esteem a power, according to rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from what we hear' swaps PRISE for the same-sounding PRIZE.
explanation.definitionFit: To prize something is to value it highly.
